t: This is the memorial to Walter Besant, a bronze bas-relief on the Victoria Embankment. Look closely at the portrait: it shows him wearing eye-glasses, which is thought to be the earliest example of that in London. Besant was an English novelist and historian. The sculptor was Sir George Frampton, a leading figure in the New Sculpture movement, who also made the Edith Cavell Memorial in London and the Peter Pan statue in Kensington Gardens.
